text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers on Monday.

* The Italian government will propose pension spending cuts of at least five trillion lire ($2.9 billion) when it meets with trades unions leaders on Tuesday to discuss welfare reform. Measures to cut spending could include raising the minimum age at which pensions can be drawn (La Repubblica).
* A survey by ISPO showed that over half of Italians are unaware of the government system proposed by the country's constitutional affairs committee.

* European Commissioner Mario Monti cautioned Prime Minister Romano Prodi that Italy was still not assured of a place in the planned single currency at its launch in 1999. He said Italy must reduce its public debt from current levels which are above limits set out in the Maastricht treaty. (La Repubblica).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
